title: TLS:support decrypt ECC_SM4_CBC_SM3 ciphersuite
description:
ECC_SM4_CBC_SM3 is defined in GB/T38636-2020   
Information security technology-Transport layer cryptography protocol   
which is a Chinese national standard.   
prf alg of ciphersuites defined in GB/T 38636-2020 are the same as TLS1.2.

notes.body:
[ECC_SM4_CBC_SM3.log](/uploads/ccf7c446281d592879b36bd6ce93153f/ECC_SM4_CBC_SM3.log)[ECC_SM4_CBC_SM3.pcapng](/uploads/223bce0888e39816b9004308fb012180/ECC_SM4_CBC_SM3.pcapng)

should use libgcrypt v1.9 or after because SM3 and SM4 are supported only in libgcrypt v1.9 or after

IMHO this is this code block that should be protected with GCRYPT_VERSION_NUMBER check to avoid calling gcrypt when it doe not support this cipher, and you should not define GCRY_MD_SM3 locally

for example,If build environment's libgcrypt is v1.8.5, and my computer install v1.9.0.
If I add guard code,though my computer satisfy v1.9.0,It'll doesn't work.
So I define GCRY_MD_SM3 locally.
what's your suggest?

That's not how we handle 3rd party libraries: what matters is the one available at compilation time.
So what happens if we exceute your new code with a libgcrypt 1.8.5 version installed?

Windows binary is compiled against libraries we distribute in the installer, Linux is compiled by the distribution maintainers or users using the libraries they target, ...
Please change you code to match what we do elsewhere.
I have uploaded new code,please review it
Please use the libgcrypt version check during compilation, as requested
update code, please review it.
@pquantin friendly ping
This change seems unrelated? Or is it also related to ECC_SM4_CBC_SM3?
this is related to ECC_SM4_CBC_SM3

ECC_SM4_CBC_SM3 is defined in GB/T38636-2020  
Information security technology-Transport layer cryptography protocol  
which is a Chinese national standard.In this standard, tls version is 
GMTLSV1_VERSION.
